$comment: THE BUNDLED DEFAULT, not the only source. See presets/README.md for the resolution chain:
plugin options -> ~/.config/lacode/pool.json -> this file -> a built-in fallback.
src/lib/pool.ts reads it at config time and rewrites every pooled variant agent
(explore-N, implement-N, context-N) plus the provider whitelists
to match, so no model is written down next to an agent anywhere.
Slot N is the same model for every base agent, which is what makes load shared.
RULES, all validated at startup: models are written provider/model-id, split on the FIRST
slash only so openrouter's vendor-prefixed ids (nvidia/x:free) resolve. A model may
appear on more than one line: each line is its own slot with its own budget.
ANY NUMBER OF SLOTS: one hidden variant per base per slot is declared from the resolved
table, and the watcher declares a variant when a reload grows the table. There is no slot cap.
WEIGHT IS THE ACTIVE-SESSION BUDGET FOR ONE PASS: a slot may hold up to its weight in
concurrent claims before the next slot is preferred. Slots are filled in declaration
order; preference is order, never weight.
Routing is ONE ordered pass: each usable slot fills up to its weight, in declaration
order. A slot is skipped when it is cooling or unavailable. When every usable slot is at
its weight, the pool is at capacity (the sum of the weights) and overflow goes to the
least-loaded usable slot; the pool never refuses work.
Live claims decide the next slot: a released claim immediately reopens its slot, and
there is no stored position.
With this file: weights 3,2,1,1 give 7 active sessions in total. To give a model more
capacity, list it again on another line with its own weight.
Equal weights give a plain pass in list order.
DECLARATION ORDER IS PREFERENCE. Slots are filled in declaration order, so the slot
you want preferred comes first; weight sets its per-pass budget, not its priority.
EVERY SLOT IS A MODEL THAT IS PROBABLY STILL THERE NEXT WEEK, AND NO TWO SLOTS
SHARE A FAMILY. A free model can be withdrawn by its provider without warning, and
a pool where every slot is one family is one withdrawal away from being empty. The
slots here are long-lived free ones spread over two providers and four model
families. If a slot does go away, the plugin warns at startup and the rest keep
working; the fix is a one-line edit here, not a redesign.
Absent means weight 1. Must be a number in (0, 100]; anything else warns and uses 1.
List order sets preference: earlier slots are preferred first, so put the slots you
want worked first at the top of the list.
COST IS THE DEFAULT, NOT A CONSTRAINT. These slots are free because that is what
the pool is FOR: mechanical work -- reading files, grepping, mechanical edits, cartography.
They are not here to be the smartest model in the system. The point of putting that work
on a near-free model is that the mechanical tokens stop being spent by your expensive
main model, and that the main model's context is never filled with file contents it does
not need to reason about. Those are two separate effects and the second is the larger one.
The pool is OPEN: it accepts any model you give it, free, cheap or expensive, and the
plugin never inspects, prices, warns about, filters or rewrites one. There is no
allowlist, no cost check, and no validation beyond structure (US-7). Free is expressed
once, right here, as the choice this file makes for you when you have not made one.
You MAY substitute your own list, including paid models, and nothing will reject or
second-guess it: edit the "slots" array below (replace a {"model": ...} entry with your
own provider/id and keep the weight), or leave this file alone entirely and put the list
in ~/.config/lacode/pool.json instead, which wins over it.
Re-check any model you substitute against models.dev; this project does not look prices
up at runtime and will not guess at them for you.
Changing this file is picked up live: the pool watches its sources, reloads the slot table and validates every slot. A restart is only needed for plugin CODE, not for a pool edit.
